tagline: Up the West Branch and over the divide.
intro: Out of Lock Haven, Route 120 follows the West Branch Susquehanna up into the mountains of Sproul State Forest to Renovo, then turns up Sinnemahoning Creek and the Driftwood Branch to Emporium, and crosses to St. Marys and Ridgway, about 100 miles in all. For much of the way the valley is a state park natural area, measured from mountain rim to mountain rim.

The road follows the Sinnemahoning Path, a Native American trail across the Eastern Continental Divide that pioneers later used as well, and that was also known as the Bucktail Trail. The byway's name belongs to the Bucktails, a Civil War rifle regiment whose men came from this country.

moments.title: Renovo
moments.text: The Philadelphia and Erie Railroad built the town as the halfway point of its line, laid it out on the river flats in a city grid and named the avenues for the Great Lakes.

moments.title: Driftwood
moments.text: A borough of 36 people where two branches of Sinnemahoning Creek meet, at the bottom of a gorge cut 1,200 feet or more into the Allegheny Plateau.

moments.title: St. Marys
moments.text: Founded in 1842 and settled mostly by Bavarian Catholics, the town has its downtown right on the Eastern Continental Divide, and the Straub Brewery is still run by the founding family.

practical: Renovo is the last place to buy fuel for many miles.
